title: Brewing coffee
lang: en

Coffee brewing is mostly a matter of controlling grind size, water temperature, and contact time. Get those three variables aligned and the result is repeatable, no matter which method you choose.

## Water temperature and grind

Aim for water between 90 and 96°C — just off the boil. Hotter water over-extracts and produces a burnt, acrid taste; cooler water under-extracts and leaves the cup sour and thin. Grind size should match the method: coarse for French press, medium for pour-over, fine for espresso. A coarser grind slows extraction, a finer one speeds it up, so grind and steep time move together.

## Extraction method

Pour-over (like V60 or Chemex) gives a clean, bright cup because paper filters trap oils and fine particles. Start with a small bloom pour — around twice the coffee weight in water — to let the grounds off-gas, then add the rest steadily over two to three minutes. French press keeps the oils in, producing a fuller, heavier body; press at four minutes and pour immediately so the grounds do not keep extracting. Both methods use roughly sixty grams of coffee per litre of water as a starting point; adjust to taste.
